correctness.rationale: Peirce decomposition exhaustively classifies radical ideals by triples U,Z,T. The forced central subspace has quotient dimension (a-u)(b-z). Every ordered product is \(U\otimes Z'\); nonzero rectangles have uniquely recoverable contraction supports. Subspace Gaussian counts, two exhaustive zero-product cases and the disjoint both-zero/both-equal-nonzero commute partition reconstruct the exact formulas. Six direct exhaustive small-prime-field checks and 175 arithmetic mass identities agree; arbitrary-field proof does not depend on these computations.

value.rationale: The invariant is the full ordered ideal multiplication map in the first radical-length family with nontrivial products; it naturally detects factorability of central ideals, exact prescribed-product fibers, missing ideal-product dimensions and the failure of commutativity. The first example has exactly 19 commuting ordered pairs among 25 radical-ideal pairs; for two arrows on each edge, dimension three is excluded from central ideal-product ranks. This complete classification across all positive arrow multiplicities and finite-field orders is not a relabeling of a known table or an unmotivated small slice.
